allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Navy Lt. Tom Farrell meets a young woman, Susan Atwell, and they share a passionate fling. Farrell then finds out that his superior, Defense Secretary David Brice, is also romantically involved with Atwell. When the young woman turns up dead, Farrell is put in charge of the murder investigation. He begins to uncover shocking clues about the case, but when details of his encounter with Susan surface, he becomes a suspect as well.

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: Assigned to head a high-stakes homicide probe, an investigator discovers that the clues he uncovers are steadily assembling a case against himself.
visibleEditorialCopy.description: After a passionate liaison with a woman who is also seeing the Secretary of Defense, Navy Lt. Tom Farrell is assigned to lead her murder inquiry, only to find the evidence pointing straight back to him.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Suspenseful and tightly wound, this steady 1987 thriller delivers moderate emotional weight and high-pressure investigative tension.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Roger Donaldson crafts a sharp, suspenseful political thriller where a military investigator must solve a homicide while actively dodging his own growing entrapment.

claudeAdvisory.claimSpan: the clues he uncovers are steadily assembling a case against himself
issueSummaries: curiosityHook says the clues Farrell uncovers are 'steadily assembling a case against himself'. The overview separates two things: he uncovers 'shocking clues about the case', and he becomes a suspect 'when details of his encounter with Susan surface'. The copy merges them and makes his own investigation the source of the evidence against him. That misassigns the causal mechanism of how he becomes a suspect.

description repeats the same causal shift with 'the evidence pointing straight back to him'. The packet ties his suspect status to his encounter with Susan coming to light, not to evidence found in the murder inquiry. 'Straight back' also adds directness and inevitability that the source does not state.
claudeAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: Most of the copy is grounded or is tolerated figurative language and genre shorthand under A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1. The exception is the recurring causal framing in curiosityHook and description, where the evidence found in the investigation incriminates Farrell. The overview instead ties his suspect status to details of his encounter with Susan surfacing. That falsely specifies plot mechanics and causality, which are named materiality categories, and it changes what a viewer would expect about how the central twist works. It does not contradict the premise, invent identities, or reveal anything beyond what the overview states, so the severity is MINOR and not SEVERE. A bounded fix would keep the two facts separate, for example 'when details of his own fling with her come to light, the investigator becomes a suspect himself'.

sourceEvidence.notes: curiosityHook and description: nothing in the overview says the clues Farrell uncovers incriminate him. The overview gives a different route to suspicion: 'when details of his encounter with Susan surface, he becomes a suspect as well'. 'Steadily assembling a case' also adds a gradual-accumulation mechanic the packet does not state.

description: the passionate liaison, Susan also being involved with the Defense Secretary, Navy Lt. Tom Farrell put in charge of the murder investigation, and his becoming a suspect all restate the overview. 'Assigned to lead' paraphrases 'put in charge of'. 'Seeing' softens 'romantically involved with'. Susan is not named, and the copy uses 'a woman' and 'her murder inquiry'. That is an emphasis choice. The suspect-status turn appears in the authorized overview, so it is not a spoiler-boundary leak.

curiosityHook and whyWatch: assignment to head a homicide investigation and the investigator becoming a suspect restate the overview. 'High-stakes' is figurative urgency. 'Military investigator' paraphrases 'Navy Lt.' put in charge of the case. 'Actively dodging his own growing entrapment' is discussed under uncertaintyNotes.

whyWatch and vibeSummary: 'political thriller' and 'thriller' are consistent with genres Drama/Thriller and the Defense Secretary premise. 'Roger Donaldson' and '1987' match director and year. 'Tightly wound' and 'high-pressure investigative tension' are tonal shorthand.

acceptedSemanticClassification: 'Suspenseful' matches moods. 'Steady' matches pace=medium. 'Moderate emotional weight' matches emotionalWeight=moderate. Keyword-only material (soviet spy, mole, espionage, photographic evidence, pentagon) is not imported.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: This is a near-threshold call. 'Evidence pointing back to him' and 'clues assembling a case against himself' could be read as loose shorthand for 'he becomes a suspect', and the overview's 'shocking clues' leave open what they show. An adjudicator could approve on that basis. I flag the fields because the overview names a specific route to suspicion (details of the encounter surfacing) and the copy replaces it with a different one. 'Actively dodging his own growing entrapment' in whyWatch adds an evasion mechanic and an implication of a deliberate trap that the packet does not state. I left it within tolerance as thematic shorthand, though a stricter reading could extend the same concern to that field. 'Seeing' for 'romantically involved with' was considered and left within tolerance.

geminiAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: All visible editorial copy strictly adheres to A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1. The narrative premise, character dynamic, and investigative trap in the description and curiosityHook faithfully track the authorized overview. Most critically, the copy demonstrates rigorous setup-only restraint: despite provocative keywords in the factual packet ('mole', 'soviet spy', 'deep cover'), the editorial text scrupulously omits all third-act identity twists, espionage revelations, and climax outcomes. Experiential descriptors in whyWatch and vibeSummary cleanly align with verified metadata and accepted semantic classifications.
